CHEYENNE WYOMING:
Section 1. That Chapter 8.29, Hood System Cleaning Companies, of Title 8, Health and
Safety, of the code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, is hereby created as set out in this
ordinance.
Chapter 8.29
HOOD SYSTEM CLEANING COMPANIES
8.29.010
Definitions.
The following definitions shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of the
following provisions relating to hood system cleaning and equipment.
"Cleaning and returning to service hood system" means servicing of the hood system,
including any or all of the following: washing, maintaining, inspecting, returning to service,
and providing documentation of the work performed.
"Commercial Cooking Appliances” means appliances used in commercial food service
fumes, smoke, or odors that are required to be removed through a local exhaust ventilation
system. Such appliances include deep fat fryers, upright broilers, griddles, broilers, steam-
jacketed kettles, hot-top ranges, underfired broilers (charbroil ers), ovens, barbecues,
rotisseries, and similar appliances. For the purpose of this definition, a food service
establishment shall include any building or portion thereof used for the preparation and serving
of food.
"Hood system" means an air-intake device used to capture by entrapment,
impingement, adhesion, or similar means, grease and similar contaminants before they enter
the duct system.The types of hood systems are:
Type I. A kitchen hood system for collection and removing grease vapors and
smoke.
Type I1.A general kitchen hood system for collecting and removing steam
vapor, heat, odors, and products of combustion.
8.29.020
Business license required.
Every company who cleans hood systems as defined by 8.29.010 is required to obtain a
business license to perform hood system cleaning. A licensed company is allowed to have one
licensed member supervise no more than three additional non-licensed employees on the same
job. An application and a non-refundable annual licensing fee of ninety dollars ($90.00) must be
submitted to the office of city clerk. Upon approval by the fire marshal, or his or her designee,
the city clerk shall issue a license which will be effective for one year from date of issuance.
General licensing provisions set forth in Chapter 5.04 of the city code apply to this type of
license.
8.29.030
Servicing and testing.
All persons licensed must clean and inspect all hood systems and equipment in
accordance with the International Fire Code, as adopted and referenced in Chapter 8.12 of the
city code.

8.29.040
Examination.
Applicants for a hood system cleaning license shall have successfully passed a written
examination administered by a recognized association or group meeting the standard of NFPA
96. The applicant must submit proof of recognized certification to be approved by the city. The
examination may be supplemented by practical tests or demonstrations deemed necessary to
determine the applicant's knowledge and ability to clean hood systems and related equipment.
The results of the examination shall be forwarded to the office of city clerk to accompany the
license application.
8.29.050
Insurance.
All persons licensed are required to maintain current general liability insurance equal to
the minimum amount required of all other contractors pursuant to the provisions of Chapter 5.44
of the city code.
8.29.060
Tagging of cleaned hood systems and related equipment.
When a licensee cleans and returns the hood system and its related equipment back into
service, a tag shall be affixed that at least states the month and year the service is performed, the
type of work completed, and the name and license number of the licensee. Further
documentation of the reported work is required to be sent to the fire prevention division of the
fire department within seven days of completed work. Only pre-approved forms meeting the
requirements of NFPA 96 and the fire prevention division of the fire department will be accepted
as documentation of work performed.
Section 2.That this ordinance shall be in full force and effect upon its approval and
publication.
